### Problem 1
## a. Download and Read File
```{r}
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/AUX_I.xpt", "AUX_I.XPT", mode = "wb")
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/DEMO_I.xpt", "DEMO_I.XPT", mode = "wb")

aux <- read_xpt("AUX_I.XPT")
demo <- read_xpt("DEMO_I.XPT")

dim(aux)
dim(demo)
names(aux)
names(demo)
```

merge into a dataframe

AUXTWIDR:	Tympanometric width, right ear

AUXTWIDL:	Tympanometric width, left ear

```{r}
attr(aux$AUXTWIDR, "label")
attr(aux$AUXTWIDL, "label")
# check these labels are about Tympanometric
summary(aux$AUXTWIDR)
summary(aux$AUXTWIDL)
# check the number of NA's
```

```{r}
aux_s <- aux[, c("SEQN", "AUXTWIDR", "AUXTWIDL")]
names(aux_s) <- c("SEQN", "tymp_r", "tymp_l")

demo_s <- demo[, c("SEQN", "RIAGENDR", "DMDCITZN", "DMDHHSZA", "INDHHIN2")]
names(demo_s) <- c("SEQN", "gender_raw", "citizen_raw", "children_raw", "income_raw")
# get data with only labels we need for AUX and demo
```

```{r}
data <- merge(
  x = aux_s, 
  y = demo_s, 
  by = "SEQN", 
  all = FALSE
)
# merge AUX and demo
```

```{r}
dim(data)
# Display the dimensions of the data.frame
```
The merged data frame contained 4592 rows and 7 columns

## b. Clean the Variables

```{r}
table(data$gender_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$citizen_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$children_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$income_raw, useNA = "always")
summary(data$tymp_r)
summary(data$tymp_l)
# check if there are any weird numbers like 999
```

```{r}
data$tymp_r <- as.numeric(data$tymp_r)
data$tymp_l <- as.numeric(data$tymp_l)

data$tymp_r[data$tymp_r %in% c(555, 777, 999)] <- NA
data$tymp_l[data$tymp_l %in% c(555, 777, 999)] <- NA
# recode special numbers as NA

data$tymp_r[!is.na(data$tymp_r) & (data$tymp_r < 0 | data$tymp_r > 499)] <- NA
data$tymp_l[!is.na(data$tymp_l) & (data$tymp_l < 0 | data$tymp_l > 499)] <- NA
# the value must be in the range of 1 ~ 499

summary(data$tymp_r)
summary(data$tymp_l)
# we check the summary again but we can see that there are no invalid value
```

```{r}
data$gender_raw[data$gender_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$gender <- factor(
  data$gender_raw, 
  levels = c(1, 2), 
  labels = c("male", "female")
)
# convert gender to a factor with informative labels.
# male is the first level

data$citizen_raw[data$citizen_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$citizen <- factor(
  data$citizen_raw, 
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("citizen", "noncitizen")
)
# convert citizenship status to a factor with informative labels.

data$children_raw[data$children_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$children <- as.numeric(data$children_raw)
data$citizen[!(data$children %in% 0: 3)] <- NA
# convert the number of young children to an ordinary numeric variable.

data$income_raw[data$income_raw %in% c(12, 13, 77, 99)] <- NA
income_midpoint <- c(
  "1"  = 2500,
  "2"  = 7500,
  "3"  = 12500,
  "4"  = 17500,
  "5"  = 22500,
  "6"  = 30000,
  "7"  = 40000,
  "8"  = 50000,
  "9"  = 60000,
  "10" = 70000,
  "14" = 87500,
  "15" = 100000
)
data$income <- unname(income_midpoint[as.character(data$income_raw)])
# convert detailed income categories to approximate dollar midpoints.
# codes 12 and 13 are broad categories that cannot be mapped uniquely.
# codes 77 and 99 are documented missing-value codes.
# all four codes therefore become NA in the continuous variable.

# replace special value in all variables with NA

table(data$gender, useNA = "always")
table(data$citizen, useNA = "always")
table(data$children, useNA = "always")
table(data$income, useNA = "always")
```
The numerical household-income codes were not ordered according to actual income. Codes 12 and 13 could not be uniquely assigned to a detailed income range and were therefore set to NA; codes 77 and 99 were also treated as missing.

## c. Fit Poisson Model

```{r}
modelrp1 <- glm(
  tymp_r ~ gender, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modelrp2 <- glm(
  tymp_r ~ gender + citizen + children + income, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modellp1 <- glm(
  tymp_l ~ gender, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modellp2 <- glm(
  tymp_l ~ gender + citizen + children + income, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
# construct four Poisson models

summary(modelrp1)
summary(modelrp2)
summary(modellp1)
summary(modellp2)
```

produce a table
```{r}
irr <- function(model, model_name){
  coef_table <- summary(model)$coefficients
  beta <- coef_table[, "Estimate"]
  se <- coef_table[, "Std. Error"]
  p_value <- coef_table[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  data.frame(
    model = model_name, 
    predictor = rownames(coef_table), 
    IRR = exp(beta), 
    CI_lower = exp(beta - 1.96 * se), 
    CI_upper = exp(beta + 1.96 * se), 
    p_value = p_value, 
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
# use a function to extract exponentiated Poisson coefficients

irr_result <- rbind(
  irr(modelrp1, "1R - Right ear: gender"), 
  irr(modelrp2, "2R - Right ear: adjusted"), 
  irr(modellp1, "1L - Left ear: gender"), 
  irr(modellp2, "2L - Right ear: adjusted")
)
# combine coefficients from four models

irr_result$`IRR (95% CI)` <- sprintf(
  "%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", 
  irr_result$IRR, 
  irr_result$CI_lower, 
  irr_result$CI_upper
)
# combine IRR, lower CI and upper CI

irr_result$`p-value` <- ifelse(
  irr_result$p_value < 0.001, 
  "<0.001", 
  sprintf("%.3f", irr_result$p_value)
)
# format p-vlaues

kable(
  irr_result[, c("model", "predictor", "IRR (95% CI)", "p-value")], 
  caption = paste("Incidence rate ratios from the", 
                  "Poisson regression models"), 
  align = c("l", "l", "c", "c")
)
# print the coefficient table
```

calculate model statistics
```{r}
pseudo_r2 <- function(model){
  1 - model$deviance / model$null.deviance
}
# define a function to calculate pseudo-R-square

model_list <- list(
  "1R: Right ear, gender" = modelrp1,
  "2R: Right ear, adjusted" = modelrp2,
  "1L: Left ear, gender" = modellp1,
  "2L: Left ear, adjusted" = modellp2
)
# store all four fitted model

model_statistics <- data.frame(
  model = names(model_list), 
  N = sapply(model_list, nobs), 
  pseudo_R2 = sapply(model_list, pseudo_r2), 
  AIC = sapply(model_list, AIC), 
  row.names = NULL
)
# calculate sample size, pseudo-R-square, and AIC

names(model_statistics)[3] <- "Deviance pseudo-R²"

kable(model_statistics, 
      caption = "Sample sizes and fit statistics for the Poisson models", 
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
# print the model-statistics table
```

## d.Compare males and females in model2L
```{r}
coefficient_2L <- summary(modellp2)$coefficients

gender_beta <- coefficient_2L["genderfemale", "Estimate"]

gender_se <- coefficient_2L["genderfemale", "Std. Error"]

gender_z <- coefficient_2L["genderfemale", "z value"]

gender_p <- coefficient_2L["genderfemale", "Pr(>|z|)"]

gender_irr <- exp(gender_beta)

gender_lower <- exp(gender_beta - 1.96 * gender_se)

gender_upper <- exp(gender_beta + 1.96 * gender_se)

gender_test <- data.frame(
  comparison = "Female vs. Male", 
  IRR = round(gender_irr, 3), 
  `95% CI lower` = round(gender_lower, 3), 
  `95% CI upper` = round(gender_upper, 3), 
  `z statistic` = round(gender_z, 3), 
  `p-value` = gender_p, 
  check.names = FALSE
)
# calculate coefficient, standard error, 
# Wald z statistics, Wald p-value, and IRR

kable(
  gender_test, 
  caption = "Model2L test of female-to-male incidence rate ratio"
)
```
In Model 2L, the female-to-male IRR was 1.019 (95% CI: [1.012, 1.026], z = 5.176, p = 2e-07). Holding the other covariates constant, females had an expected left-ear tympanometric width that was 1.019 times that of males. Because p was less than .05, there was sufficient evidence of a gender difference.

```{r}
modellp2_data <- model.frame(modellp2)
# obtain data used to fit model 2L

prediction_data <- data.frame(
  gender = factor(
    c("male", "female"), 
    levels = levels(modellp2_data$gender)
  ), 
  citizen = factor(
    c("citizen", "citizen"), 
    levels = levels(modellp2_data$citizen)
  ), # use only citizen because the difference we want is gender
  children = rep(
    mean(modellp2_data$children), 
    2
  ), 
  income = rep(
    mean(modellp2_data$income), 
    2
  )
)
# generate new data with different gender

prediction_data

pred_link <- predict(
  modellp2, 
  newdata = prediction_data, 
  type = "link", 
  se.fit = TRUE
)
# predict on the log scale

prediction_data$predicted <- exp(pred_link$fit)

prediction_data$lower <- exp(pred_link$fit - 1.96 * pred_link$se.fit)

prediction_data$upper <- exp(pred_link$fit + 1.96 * pred_link$se.fit)

prediction_table <- data.frame(
  gender = prediction_data$gender, 
  `adjusted predicted value` = prediction_data$predicted, 
  `95% CI lower` = prediction_data$lower, 
  `95% CI upper` = prediction_data$upper, 
  check.names = FALSE
)
# calculate the original outcome and 95% CI

kable(
  prediction_table, 
  caption = "Adjusted predicted left-ear Tympanometric width from model 2L"
)

```

```{r}
prediction_male <- prediction_data$predicted[
    prediction_data$gender == "male"
  ]

prediction_female <- prediction_data$predicted[
    prediction_data$gender == "female"
  ]
# extract predictions for males and females

prediction_diff <- prediction_female - prediction_male

prediction_ratio <- prediction_female / prediction_male
# calculate the predicted difference and ratio

prediction_comp_df <- data.frame(
  statistics = c(
    "adjusted prediction: male", 
    "adjusted prediction: female", 
    "female minus male", 
    "female devided by male", 
    "Wald z statistic for equality", 
    "Wald p-value for equality"
  ), 
  value = c(
    prediction_male, 
    prediction_female, 
    prediction_diff, 
    prediction_ratio, 
    gender_z, 
    gender_p
  )
)

kable(
  prediction_comp_df, 
  caption = "comparison of adjusted predicted values from model 2L"
)
```
With citizenship fixed at Citizen and the continuous covariates held at their Model 2L sample means, the predicted left-ear tympanometric width was 83.85024 for males and 85.42727 for females. The female-minus-male difference was 1.5770302. The test produced z = 2.1764513 and p = 0.0000002; therefore, the predicted values [did/did not] differ significantly between males and females.

### Problem 2 - Sakila

load library and database
```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(dplyr)
library(microbenchmark)

sakila <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "sakila_master.db")
```

## a. Number of customers and percentage of customers are active
Use R for calculation
```{r}
customers <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT store_id, active
  FROM customer
  "
) # retrieve each customer's store ID and active status from the database.

ans_aR <- customers %>%
  group_by(store_id) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_customers = n(),
    percent_active = 100 * mean(active == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# group customers by store
# count total number of customers 
# calculate the percentage of active customers
ans_aR
```

Use SQL for calculation
```{r}
ans_aSQL <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila, 
  "
  SELECT 
    store_id, 
    COUNT(*) AS number_of_customers, 
    100.0 * SUM(active) / COUNT(*) AS active_percentage
  FROM CUSTOMER
  GROUP BY store_id
  ORDER BY store_id
  "
) # select store id, number of rows, and sum of active(which is 0 or 1) divided by number of rows
ans_aSQL
```

## b. identify the names and country of staff
Use R for calculation
```{r}
staff_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT staff_id, first_name, last_name, address_id
  FROM staff
  "
)

address_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT address_id, city_id
  FROM address
  "
)

city_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT city_id, country_id
  FROM city
  "
)

country_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT country_id, country
  FROM country
  "
)
# retrieve staff, address, city, country information.
# address_id will be used to connect each staff member to an address.

answer_bR <- staff_df %>%
  left_join(address_df, by = "address_id") %>%
  left_join(city_df, by = "city_id") %>%
  left_join(country_df, by = "country_id") %>%
  transmute(
    staff_id,
    name = paste(first_name, last_name),
    country
  ) %>%
  arrange(staff_id)
# join the four tables in R
answer_bR
```

Use SQL for calculation
```{r}
ans_bSQL <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila, 
  "
  SELECT
    staff.staff_id, 
    staff.first_name, 
    staff.last_name, 
    country.country
  FROM STAFF AS staff
  JOIN ADDRESS AS address
    ON staff.address_id = address.address_id
  JOIN CITY as city
    ON address.city_id = city.city_id
  JOIN COUNTRY AS country
    ON city.country_id = country.country_id
  ORDER BY staff.staff_id
  "
) # to get country, we have to connect STAFF-ADDRESS-CITY-COUNTRY
ans_bSQL
```

## c. identify the names of the films
Use R for calculation
```{r}
film_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT film_id, title
  FROM film
  "
)

inventory_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT inventory_id, film_id
  FROM inventory
  "
)

rental_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT rental_id, inventory_id
  FROM rental
  "
)

payment_df <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila,
  "
  SELECT payment_id, rental_id, amount
  FROM payment
  "
)
# retrieve film IDs and titles, inventory records, rental records, payment records

film_revenue_R <- payment_df %>%
  inner_join(rental_df, by = "rental_id") %>%
  inner_join(inventory_df, by = "inventory_id") %>%
  inner_join(film_df, by = "film_id") %>%
  group_by(film_id, title) %>%
  summarise(
    total_rental_value = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# combine the tables using payment-rental-inventory-film

answer_cR <- film_revenue_R %>%
  filter(total_rental_value == max(total_rental_value)) %>%
  arrange(title)
# find the film with the largest total rental value

answer_cR
```

Use SQL for calculation
```{r}
ans_cSQL <- dbGetQuery(
  sakila, 
  "
  WITH film_revenue AS (
      SELECT
          f.film_id,
          f.title,
          SUM(p.amount) AS total_rental_value
      FROM film AS f
      JOIN inventory AS i
        ON f.film_id = i.film_id
      JOIN rental AS r
        ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
      JOIN payment AS p
        ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
      GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title
  )
  SELECT
      film_id,
      title,
      total_rental_value
  FROM film_revenue
  WHERE total_rental_value = (
      SELECT MAX(total_rental_value)
      FROM film_revenue
  )
  ORDER BY title
  "
)
# combine the tables using payment-rental-inventory-film
# keep the film whose revenue equals the maximum

ans_cSQL
```

## Benchmark
benchmark for a
```{r}
set.seed(123)
benchmark_a <- microbenchmark(
  R_method = {
    customers <- dbGetQuery(
      sakila,
      "
      SELECT store_id, active
      FROM customer
      "
    )
    
    ans_aR <- customers %>%
      group_by(store_id) %>%
      summarise(
        number_of_customers = n(),
        percent_active = 100 * mean(active == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }, 
  SQL_method = {
    ans_aSQL <- dbGetQuery(
      sakila, 
      "
      SELECT 
        store_id, 
        COUNT(*) AS number_of_customers, 
        100.0 * SUM(active) / COUNT(*) AS active_percentage
      FROM CUSTOMER
      GROUP BY store_id
      ORDER BY store_id
      "
    )
  }, 
  times = 100L
)
# compare two methods in (a) using benchmark
summary(benchmark_a)
```

benchmark for c
```{r}
set.seed(123)
benchmark_c <- microbenchmark(
  R_method = {
    film_df <- dbGetQuery(

      FROM film
      "
    )
    
    inventory_df <- dbGetQuery(

      FROM payment
      "
    )
    
    film_revenue_R <- payment_df %>%
      inner_join(rental_df, by = "rental_id") %>%
      inner_join(inventory_df, by = "inventory_id") %>%
      inner_join(film_df, by = "film_id") %>%
      group_by(film_id, title) %>%
      summarise(
        total_rental_value = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"

    answer_cR <- film_revenue_R %>%
      filter(total_rental_value == max(total_rental_value)) %>%
      arrange(title)
  }, 
  SQL_method = {
    ans_cSQL <- dbGetQuery(
      sakila, 
      "
      WITH film_revenue AS (
          SELECT
              f.film_id,
              f.title,
              SUM(p.amount) AS total_rental_value
          FROM film AS f
          JOIN inventory AS i
            ON f.film_id = i.film_id
          JOIN rental AS r
            ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
          JOIN payment AS p
            ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
          GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title
      )
      SELECT
          film_id,
          title,
          total_rental_value
      FROM film_revenue
      WHERE total_rental_value = (
          SELECT MAX(total_rental_value)
          FROM film_revenue
      )
      ORDER BY title
      "
    )
  }, 
  times = 100L
)
# compare two methods in (c) using benchmark
summary(benchmark_c)
```
The benchmark results show that the SQL approach had shorter execution time than the approach that extracted the tables and performed the joins and calculations in R.

## d. cell phone format
```{r}
# define a function that reformats phone number
phone_format <- function(x){
  digits <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", x)
  good <- !is.na(x) & nchar(digits) == 10
  result <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  result[good] <- paste0(
    substr(digits[good], 1, 4), "-", 
    substr(digits[good], 5, 7), "-", 
    substr(digits[good], 8, 10)
  )
  result
}

cell_phone1 <- phone_format(data_au[["phone1"]])
cell_phone2 <- phone_format(data_au[["phone2"]])
head(cell_phone1, 10)
head(cell_phone2, 10)
# print the first ten phone numbers from both columns

```

## e. histogram of apartment number
```{r}
address <- trimws(data_au[["address"]])
# remove unnecessary spaces from the addresses
has_num_address <- grepl("[0-9]+$", address)
# check the addresses have apartment number or not
apt_num <- rep(NA_real_, length(address))
# create a output vector
apt_num[has_num_address] <- as.numeric(
  sub(".*?([0-9]+)$", "\\1", address[has_num_address])
) # extract the sequence of digits of apartment number
head(data.frame(address, apt_num), 10)
```

```{r}
valid_apt <- !is.na(apt_num) & apt_num > 0
# zero must be excluded because log(0) is undefined

hist(
  log(apt_num[valid_apt]), 
  breaks = "FD", 
  main = "Histogram of Log Apartment Numbers", 
  xlab = "log(apartment number)", 
  col = "lightblue", 
  border = "white"
) # draw the histogram of observed digits without NA and 0
```

## f. examine Benford’s law
```{r}
first_digit <- as.integer(
  substr(as.character(apt_num[!is.na(apt_num) & apt_num > 0]), 1, 1)
)

observed_prop <- prop.table(
  table(factor(first_digit, levels = 1: 9))
)
observed_prop # get first digit of apartment number

benford_prop <- log10(1 + 1 / 1: 9) # get the distribution of benford's law

benford_table <- data.frame(
  digit = 1: 9, 
  observed = as.numeric(observed_prop), 
  benford = benford_prop
) # merge into a dataframe
benford_table
```

```{r}
barplot(
  rbind(
    observed = benford_table$observed, 
    benford = benford_table$benford
  ), 
  beside = TRUE, 
  names.arg = 1: 9, 
  xlab = "Leading digit", 
  ylab = "Proportion", 
  main = "Apartment Numbers vs. Benford's Law", 
  col = c("steelblue", "red")
) # drawing barplot of observed digits and Benford's law

legend(
  "topright", 
  legend = c("observed", "benford"), 
  fill = c("steelblue", "red"), 
  bty = "n"
)
```

$H_0$: The leading digits follow Benford's law.

$H_A$: The leading digits do not follow Benford's law.
```{r}
benford_test <- chisq.test(
  x = as.numeric(table(factor(first_digit, levels = 1:9))),
  p = benford_prop
) # doing hypothesis test

benford_test
```
